content:
zoe: Heads up — ACME reported 3 failed invoice charges in a row. customer_id=acme-inc, payment_id=pay_0A1B2C, card_last4=4242, scheme=visa. They get a 3DS challenge but it never completes, then we see acquirer timeout and final decline.
manuel: Can you paste the gateway responses? rough logs are fine.
zoe: Paste from our proxy logs: 
```
2026-03-12T16:02:18Z request_id=req_9f1a status=attempting_3ds -> redirect_to_acs
2026-03-12T16:02:38Z request_id=req_9f1a acs_response=timeout acquirer_gateway=adriatic-payments code=402 detail="ACS timeout while waiting for challenge result"
2026-03-12T16:02:38Z request_id=req_9f1a final_status=declined decline_reason=3DS_AUTHENTICATION_FAILED
```
zoe: They say this only started ~24h ago. Customer tried in EU region and US region with same result.
payments_oncall: Reproduced once in staging with a simulator — ACS sometimes redirects then never posts result back. Looks like intermittent ACS postback loss or merchant redirect flow dropping.
fraud_ops: From fraud side, we did raise a passive risk flag on the customer due to velocity, but nothing that should force a hard decline on our side. The decline is coming from acquirer/gateway (402) not internal fraud module.
emma: Do we have the exact charge request we sent to the gateway (headers + body)? need to check 3ds version and timeout param.
zoe: Repro curl we gave the merchant (sanitized):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/payments/charge \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_XXXXX" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"amount":19900,"currency":"EUR","payment_method":{"type":"card","token":"tok_abc"},"return_url":"https://acme.example/3ds/return"}'
```
zoe: No explicit 3ds_timeout param in that payload — relying on gateway default (10s).
manuel: Gateway notes show acquirer ACS took ~15-18s to respond in some attempts; our default 10s < ACS response -> we treat as timeout then gateway issues decline.
payments_oncall: Immediate mitigation: ask merchant to set return_url to a reachable page that posts result quickly, and suggest they allow a longer ACS session. We can also raise our gateway timeout to 25s for this merchant as emergency.
fraud_ops: Recommend a controlled retry policy: if acquirer returns ACS timeout, schedule one automated retry within 30s; but need to avoid duplicate capture in edge cases.
emma: I can push a short config flag to increase acquirer timeout per-merchant in the routing layer. Will require a small hotfix and an audit entry.
deploy-bot: Deploy pipeline: payment-routing-service v2.11.4 -> canary in eu-west-1 scheduled if PR approved.
zoe: Customer asked for timeline. Can we 1) confirm cause, 2) do a quick fix?
manuel: Root cause likely: ACS/issuer handling increased latency (15-20s) + our gateway default timeout (10s) -> acquirer marks as failed. We'll patch per-merchant timeout and revert after ACS stabilizes.
payments_oncall: Action items: @emma create PR to add merchant-specific acs_timeout (default 10s, override up to 30s) + metrics for ACS postback latency. @fraud_ops confirm no rule will block retries. @zoe confirm with merchant they can accept longer ACS flows.
zoe: I'll ask merchant to test with the staging curl and share a network HAR if it fails again.
fraud_ops: Also flagging possible bot/automation at issuer — if we see many half-complete flows from same card, escalate to the issuer via acquirer.
emma: PR ready for review, will add audit logs and a canary toggle. ETA for canary: ~3 hours after approval.
zoe: Thanks. I'll hold off refunds / retries until we have the config change in place and merchant confirmation. :thumbsup:
manuel: One more note — merchant reported two attempts where 3DS challenge returned an error ‘user_cancelled’. Could be UX confusion. Recommend merchant UX updates to show spinner and prevent premature nav.
zoe: Good call, I'll pass that to their devs.
payments_oncall: If we need to be faster, I can manually flip the merchant-level timeout flag after PR merge.
zoe: OK marking as high priority. Will update thread with merchant HAR and any new logs.
